case_name: Prakash Kumar Bachlaus vs Smt. Chanchal @ Jaya
facts_of_case: Marriage took place on 30.11.1993, wife left the matrimonial home on 14.5.1994, husband sought annulment of marriage due to fraud and wife's mental disorder.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage can be annulled if the wife was suffering from a serious mental disorder that rendered living together impossible.
legal_principles.held: In view of the clear findings of the Family Court that the respondent wife was suffering from such serious mental disorder as to render of the living together of the husband and wife impossible
cited_cases: Durga Prasanna Tripathy v. Arundhati Tripathy
Bikkar Singh v. Smt. Mohinder Kaur AIR 1981 Punjab & Haryana 391
Smt. Asha Srivastava v. R.K. Srivastava AIR 1981 Delhi 253
use_in: divorce cases where mental health is an issue

legal_principles.principle: A marriage can be annulled if the parties have lived separately for more than 12 years and there is no possibility of reconciliation.
legal_principles.held: Having lived separately for more than 12 years now, the marriage had fallen on the rocks and had crossed the point of return
use_in: divorce cases where separation has been long-standing

outcome.final_order: Decree of annulment denied due to husband continuing to live with wife after knowing about her mental disorder.
